newsitem.title: FRANCE: French strike to hit European air traffic Thursday.
newsitem.headline: French strike to hit European air traffic Thursday.

text.p: A strike by French air controllers and staff at airlines Air France and Air Inter Europe is set to disrupt air traffic in Europe on Thursday when public sector workers protest against the government's austerity budget.
French flag-carrier Air France said on Tuesday it would maintain all its long-haul flights but medium-haul flights could be affected.
"We will assure all our long-distance flights," an Air France spokeswoman said. But medium-haul destinations will be badly hit although details were still being finalised.

Air France has not received any strike notices for Thursday, but the airline has to comply with the French DGAC civil aviation authority's request to cut non-essential flights due to a minimum service in air traffic control on the day.
In long-haul, Air France handles an average 100 return flights a day, and about 300 medium-haul, the spokeswoman said.
Air Inter Europe, the domestic and regional airline in the Air France group will fly only 110 out of a total 500 flights on Thursday.
The Direction Generale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC) has asked all airlines to cut flights to and from France to 15 percent of normal service, in view of the reduced air traffic control.
That reduced service represents around 500 flights, for which there should be no delays, a DGAC spokesman said.
If there are any delays, these should be limited to overflights, expected to be around 2,000 on the day, as domestic services will have already suffered disruption due to cancellations, he said.

The controllers' strike will mean probably only about 100 flights will get away from Paris Orly airport on Thursday instead of the usual 750, with just over 100 from the main Roissy Charles De Gaulle airport instead of 1,100 at this time of year, aviation sources said.
Overflights from north to south Europe and vice-versa could be delayed, as well as flights from London.
The aviation authorities are treating cargo and express services as priorities, which was not the case in a strike by controllers last year, one official said.
Employees of Aeroports de Paris (ADP), the state-owned agency which runs Paris airports, are due to strike on Wednesday but this was not expected to disrupt flights on the day.
Strikers plan a demonstration in front of the ADP headquarters in central Paris on Wednesday morning.

French civil servants and public sector employees including teachers, defence and transport workers are striking to protest against the government's 1997 austerity budget which freezes spending and cuts around 6,000 civil service jobs.
